newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Sept S&P 500 futures finish down slightly.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sept S&P 500 futures finish down slightly.

text.p: U.S. September Standard and Poor's 500 futures ended slightly lower after late Nasdaq losses spilled into the quiet S&P 500 pit.
An S&P 500 futures trader said the market was just "treading water" ahead of this week's big economic line-up until Nasdaq losses shook weak longs out of the market.
"They were taking profits in the big winners -- IBM, Intel, Microsoft," the trader said.
But traders said volume was very light during the session as players remained wary of adding to their positions ahead of this week's economic line-up.

The second quarter U.S. employment cost index will be released on Tuesday and is forecast up 0.8 percent, compared with an 0.6 percent gain in the previous report. A quarterly refunding announcement on Wednesday and second quarter gross domestic product on Thursday precede key employment data on Friday.
A Reuters poll of economists showed an average forecast of July jobs up 193,000, versus a 217,000 June gain. The jobless rate was seen at 4.9 percent, down from 5.0 percent in June.
September S&P 500s fell through Friday's session low of 940.80 late in the day, after all day within Friday's range.
But for the most part, the market remains on hold until the economic news unfolds, traders said.
One trader said locals were September S&P 500 sellers late and a foreign bank was a featured seller after bond futures closed.
At the close, Sept S&P 500s were down 1.25 pts to 943.65, Nikkei rose 185.0 pts to 20,650.0, Midcap 400s fell 0.05 to 309.05, Russell rose 0.85 to 411.10, and NASDAQ fell 9.25 to 1083.25.
